subsystems.name: Propulsion
subsystems.role: cross the vast distances between stars.

subsystems.name: Power
subsystems.role: supply energy for mining, refining, fabrication and propulsion.

subsystems.name: Mining and refining
subsystems.role: extract and process local material into usable feedstock.

subsystems.name: Fabrication and assembly
subsystems.role: turn refined material into new probe parts and whole copies.

subsystems.name: Control and autonomy
subsystems.role: navigate, make decisions and manage the replication cycle without human help.

subsystems.name: Communication
subsystems.role: report findings and receive updates across light-years.

buildSteps.title: Design for closure
buildSteps.detail: List every component and decide whether it can be made from asteroid or moon material; plan to stockpile only the hardest items, such as advanced microchips.

buildSteps.title: Build the seed craft
buildSteps.detail: Integrate propulsion, power, mining, refining, fabrication and control into a single spacecraft, likely assembled in orbit from multiple launches.

buildSteps.title: Launch and cruise
buildSteps.detail: Use fusion or beamed energy to accelerate to a few percent of light speed; the journey to the nearest stars would take decades to centuries.

buildSteps.title: Arrive and survey
buildSteps.detail: Slow down and scan the target system for resource-rich asteroids or moons.

buildSteps.title: Establish a base
buildSteps.detail: Land or anchor on a resource body, deploy mining robots and power systems.

buildSteps.title: Mine and refine
buildSteps.detail: Extract metals, silicon and volatiles; process them into feedstock for manufacturing.

buildSteps.title: Manufacture a copy
buildSteps.detail: Use additive manufacturing and robotic assembly to build a new seed craft, testing each subsystem as it is completed.

buildSteps.title: Launch the copy
buildSteps.detail: Send the new probe to another star system; the original continues exploring or building more copies.

buildSteps.title: Repeat
buildSteps.detail: Each copy repeats the cycle, producing exponential growth in the number of probes.

prerequisites.why: no engine can yet reach another star in a reasonable time.
no machine can yet copy itself from raw materials.
current robots need human supervision; a probe must operate alone for centuries.
small-scale in-situ resource use has been demonstrated, but full mining and refining are not at scale.
needed for long journeys, though performance is limited.
radio and laser links work over interplanetary distances, but not yet over light-years.

pathway.milestone: robotic asteroid mining and in-space manufacturing experiments
pathway.unlocks: basic techniques for using local material.

pathway.milestone: self-replicating factories in Earth orbit or on the Moon, achieving partial closure
pathway.unlocks: ability to build most of a probe off Earth.

pathway.milestone: interstellar precursor probes, such as laser-sail concepts, reach the nearest stars and send back data
pathway.unlocks: proof of long-duration autonomy and communication.

pathway.milestone: first Von Neumann probe seed launched to a nearby star system

pathway.unlocks: exponentially growing coverage of the galaxy, if no physical barrier stops it.
